sarah (acme-corp): Hey team — since yesterday our production calls to Redwood are routing to us-west and adding ~250ms. Some requests are failing with 502 occasionally. Our infra team hasn't changed model config. Can you advise?

jess (support): Sorry about that — can you paste an example request id or a curl we can repro with? Also, is this on your Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated?

sarah (acme-corp): Private (VPC) deployment, running in our EU datacenter. Example request id: req_20260330_9f1b. Quick curl we used: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate` — latency shows ~320ms sometimes, errors: 502 Bad Gateway.

jess (support): Thanks — can you run `curl -s https://ipinfo.io/json` from the host that makes requests and paste the `ip` + `region` fields? We suspect egress IP might be in a different region which causes our smart-routing to pick us-west.

sarah (acme-corp): Got it, output from one of our app hosts: ```{
  "ip": "34.210.12.45",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "country": "US"
}``` — but the host is physically in NL. We have a bastion/proxy cluster in front of our app that handles peering to the cloud provider.

jess (support): That matches our hypothesis. Our routing picks region based on egress IP. I'll escalate to oncall. @raj can you take a look?

raj (oncall-eng): On it. Can you also run `traceroute api.redwood.example.com` from the same host and paste first 12 hops? Also `sudo tcpdump -nni any host api.redwood.example.com and port 443 -c 200` would be ideal (pcap attached) if you can.

sarah (acme-corp): Traceroute (trimmed): ```1 10.0.0.1 0.2 ms 0.1 ms 0.1 ms
2 10.1.1.1 1.2 ms 1.1 ms 1.0 ms
3 192.168.254.1 3.5 ms 3.6 ms 3.5 ms
4 34.210.12.1 12.3 ms 12.4 ms 12.5 ms
5 * * *
6 52.95.23.10 60.2 ms 59.9 ms 60.1 ms
...
```
I can attach a pcap if you need.

raj (oncall-eng): Traceroute shows traffic leaving local network to an egress gateway with public IP 34.210.12.45 (same as ipinfo). That IP geolocates to us-west. Likely your peering gateway or NAT is SNATing to a US egress pool. That explains the region selection.

mika (network-eng): Quick checklist: is the egress handled by a cloud-provider NAT gateway in a us-west AZ? Or do you have a centralized egress appliance in the US? Also, are you doing 1:1 SNAT on your peering appliance?

sarah (acme-corp): We use a transit peering setup. There's a legacy bastion cluster in us-west for management tooling that recently had a public NAT entry; some traffic from EU app nodes goes via peering tunnel for failover. We didn't expect app egress to hairpin through it.

jess (support): Ok that maps. Two immediate impacts: 1) higher latency because route goes to us-west; 2) our billing and model routing consider region = us-west, so usage is billed/executed there. We'll need billing/ops to mark this as misrouted. @billing-bot flag for review?

billing-bot: Noted. Opening billing ticket BLG-20260330-42 to prevent invoicing surprises while support investigates.

raj (oncall-eng): For repro steps we used: 1) Confirm egress IP: `curl -s https://ipinfo.io/ip` 2) Confirm that token is same but routing differs: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -o /tmp/resp -w "%{time_total}\n"` 3) Check if requests include an `X-Forwarded-For` or if your proxy rewrites source. If your proxy uses SNAT, our control plane only sees the NAT IP.

sarah (acme-corp): Our proxy does not set X-Forwarded-For for internal traffic; config is old. Example iptables SNAT line on their gateway: ```-A POSTROUTING -t nat -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 34.210.12.45```

mika (network-eng): That's the culprit. Two options: A) preserve client source ip using `NETMAP` or avoid SNAT for egress to Redwood IP ranges, or B) add a route so EU app hosts egress directly to internet through regional NAT. Also you can configure the proxy to append `X-Client-Region` header and not SNAT.

jess (support): While they fix network, I can set a temporary per-tenant override to force EU model routing for acme-corp so latency/billing are correct. That requires a config change on our control plane — tagging customer with `preferred_region=eu-central-1` for their token. Would that help?

sarah (acme-corp): Yes please, that would reduce latency immediately. But we still want the network fix.

raj (oncall-eng): Agreed. For long-term: network fix + we should update our routing fallback policy to check `X-Client-Region` or `X-Forwarded-For` if present and trusted (private deployments). Filing internal task RGW-546: accept trusted egress headers for region selection when `deployment_type=private`.

mika (network-eng): For customer's immediate network change, suggest adding iptables rule to bypass SNAT for redwood egress: ```-t nat -A POSTROUTING -d 3.8.0.0/16 -j RETURN``` (replace with Redwood egress ranges) — or add `--to-source` exceptions.

sarah (acme-corp): Our infra team applied a bypass rule for redwood IP ranges and restarted the proxy. Re-ran `curl -s https://ipinfo.io/json` -> ```{ "ip": "3.8.12.9", "region": "eu-central-1" }``` — now latency down to ~25ms. No more 502s so far.

jess (support): Great. I've applied `preferred_region=eu-central-1` override temporarily and asked billing to hold billing changes until this is confirmed. Removing the temporary override will be scheduled after your network change is stable.

billing-bot: BLG-20260330-42 updated: billing hold until 2026-04-06 or until support confirms resolution.

raj (oncall-eng): Action items: 1) acme-corp to keep egress bypass rule and confirm over 24h. 2) mika to add docs snippet for private deployments warning about SNAT/peering impacts. 3) platform to implement RGW-546 (trusted egress headers).

mika (network-eng): I'll draft the doc and share. Also note: customers using transit peering should avoid routing prod egress through management gateways.

sarah (acme-corp): Thanks all, feel free to close once hold is lifted. Really appreciate the fast response :thumbsup:

jess (support): Marking resolved pending 24h confirmation. Closing the support thread once sarah confirms. :white_check_mark:
